review_notes: I read the whole file and its simp attributes. I checked how the simp lemmas for diagramPushforward, diagramPushforwardCone and their projections interact. I grepped for uses of the shadowed lemmas: the only external uses I found are an explicit term-mode use in SheafCohomologyExamples/DiagramPushforward.lean line 39 and docs. I did not run Lean. The shadowing claim relies on simp's default behaviour of simplifying subterms before applying post lemmas, so I could not confirm it experimentally. I found no loops. diagramPushforwardHom_id and diagramPushforwardHom_comp are deliberately left non-simp, which looks reasonable because their statements carry dependent proof arguments.

findings.declaration: diagramPushforward_obj_carrier / diagramPushforward_obj_sheaf / diagramPushforward_map_base (and diagramPushforwardCone_carrier / diagramPushforwardCone_sheaf / diagramPushforwardCone_projection_base)
findings.problem: The simp set has a layered, competing structure. `diagramPushforward_obj` and `diagramPushforward_map` are @[simp] and rewrite `(diagramPushforward A N Y f).obj i` and `.map a` to `diagramPushforwardObj` and `diagramPushforwardHom`. They are the innermost subterms of the left-hand sides of `diagramPushforward_obj_carrier`, `diagramPushforward_obj_sheaf` and `diagramPushforward_map_base`. Simp simplifies subterms before applying post lemmas, so those inner terms should be rewritten first. The outer projection lemmas `diagramPushforwardObj_carrier`, `diagramPushforwardObj_sheaf` and `diagramPushforwardHom_base` then do the job. The three compound lemmas therefore look unreachable by simp. The same holds for the cone lemmas `diagramPushforwardCone_carrier` and `diagramPushforwardCone_sheaf`, because `diagramPushforwardCone_pt` rewrites `.pt` first. `diagramPushforwardCone_projection_base` is shadowed likewise, because `diagramPushforwardCone_projection` rewrites `.π.app i` first. These are redundant simp entries, and they give two candidate normal forms for the same expression.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one canonical route. The route already in place is: unfold `diagramPushforward.obj/.map` and `diagramPushforwardCone.pt/.π.app` once, then apply the `diagramPushforwardObj_*` and `diagramPushforwardHom_base` lemmas. Under that route, drop @[simp] from `diagramPushforward_obj_carrier`, `diagramPushforward_obj_sheaf`, `diagramPushforward_map_base`, `diagramPushforwardCone_carrier`, `diagramPushforwardCone_sheaf` and `diagramPushforwardCone_projection_base`. Keep them as plain named lemmas for `rw` and `exact`. The other option is to keep them as the direct normal-form lemmas and make the intermediate `diagramPushforward_obj/_map` and `diagramPushforwardCone_pt/_projection` lemmas non-simp. Either way the simp set then has one rewrite path per expression.
findings.benefit: The simp set is smaller and its normal form is predictable. There are no dead simp lemmas to mislead readers into thinking `simp` uses the direct statements. Simp's lemma-lookup work is also reduced slightly. Downstream users can reason about one canonical form for `.sheaf`, carrier and base projections of the pushforward diagram and cone.
